messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert: spike in 5xxs observed across hosted API. Error rate up 12% in the last 3m, concentrated on /v1/chat and /v1/rerank. Embeddings endpoints are within normal bounds. Paging on-call: @jenna_oncall :rotating_light:
jenna_oncall: I'm on it — checking ingress and runtime metrics now. Can someone grab recent deploys?
arman: no recent deploys to inference runtime in last hour. Looks like sudden request surge from a single org (org_id: org-9f3).
priya: confirming — NAT pool shows traffic spike from a handful of IPs in us-east1, high concurrency to chat.
luis: support seeing ~8 customer tickets referencing delayed responses and 500s, mostly on chat. One enterprise customer reporting production impact.
jenna_oncall: initial impact assessment: high latency -> downstream timeouts -> 5xx. We should mitigate live traffic to protect overall fleet. Propose per-endpoint temporary rate limits: reduce /v1/chat to 20 rps org-wide, set /v1/rerank to 5 rps, leave embeddings unchanged. Thoughts?
arman: +1. Targeting chat first makes sense — it's the hot path. Also enable token-based soft quota for the org causing spike. If flow continues, we can fall back their requests to smaller model variant.
priya: i'll push a route-specific policy now. Applying config to edge: route_match: "/v1/chat" -> qps:20, burst:40, scope: org-9f3.
priya: applying change...
priya: (deploy bot) config-deploy: started by priya at 2026-03-15T16:02:10Z
priya: (deploy bot) config-deploy: success — policy active across edge nodes in ~18s.
priya: snippet of policy applied:
```json
{
  "policy_name": "temp-rate-limit-org-9f3-chat",
  "route": "/v1/chat",
  "scope": "org-9f3",
  "qps": 20,
  "burst": 40,
  "duration": "15m",
  "applied_by": "priya"
}
```
arman: also added a rerank cap at the control plane: 
```yaml
route: /v1/rerank
default_qps: 2
override:
  org-9f3: 5
```
arman: pushed and active.
luis: flagged affected tickets with mitigation note and ETA 15m; escalated to enterprise SEs for the one customer.
maya_cs: notified top-10 customers via status page and directly reached out to the impacted enterprise. They want a postmortem if this persists beyond the mitigation window.
jenna_oncall: monitoring latency/5xx now. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/inference/alerts/2212345678 — watching p50/p95/p99 and error-rate.
talia_devex: Heads-up: if we route fallback to smaller model, we need devex to update SDK behavior for model downgrade messaging. I can prepare message templates.
arman: We should also enable KV-prefix caching for that org's repeated prompts; that may reduce load if they are re-sending same prefixes. But that's a longer change. For now, rate limits + rerank cap should relieve backend.
priya: fine-grained traffic shaping in place. Current cluster CPU for runtime dropped by ~30% since rate-limit applied, 5xxs trending down.
priya: metrics: error-rate /v1/chat: 12% -> 1.8% in 8m, latency p95 down from 1.8s -> 430ms.
jenna_oncall: good progress. I'm going to do a 30m watch. If stable, we'll lift org-specific limits gradually. Anyone taking handoff after me?
talia_devex: I can take the handoff at +30. Notes: mitigation active, org-9f3 limited to chat qps=20 and rerank qps=5; embedding unaffected. Support/CS notified. Follow-up actions: check for repeated patterns from org-9f3, consider permanent quota if abuse.
jenna_oncall: handing off to @talia_devex. Leaving runbook link and quick checklist: https://runbooks.redwood/mitigations/per-endpoint-quota.md — steps 1-5 done.
incident-bot: escalation log: P1 -> mitigated by route-specific rate-limits. Actions: chat qps=20 (org-9f3), rerank qps=5 (org-9f3), config deployed by priya/arman. Monitoring window started.
jenna_oncall: closing my active page. tagging this thread with #mitigation #rate-limit #handoff.
talia_devex: acknowledging handoff, will post update at +15 and +30.
jenna_oncall: thanks team :thumbsup:"
